diff --git a/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats b/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..afae0f03
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/unit/guard-yield.bats
@@ -0,0 +1,201 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/guard-yield.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD FR-1 AC-1.2 … AC-1.4,
+# SDD D-1.3, D-1.4)
+# guard-yield.sh over a fixture audit log and a rotated segment, at a fixed
+# --now: replay exclusion (flag, cwd, burst) counted in the header, the
+# likely-false-positive heuristic (heredoc, outside-repo cwd, prose class without
+# a destructive verb at statement start), day-granular last_real_catch, the
+# --check drift gate (0 after generation, 1 after an origin edit, 0 after a
+# yield-only change), the --json shape, and no command text or cwd in any output.
+# =============================================================================
+
+NOW="2026-10-14T12:00:00Z"
+
+setup() {
+  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
+  ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd -P)"
+  GY="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gyield.XXXXXX")"
+  T="$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)"
+  mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/scratch"
+  # A temp prefix the fixture controls (the script's own mktemp also uses it).
+  export TMPDIR="$T"
+  cp "$ROOT/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml" "$T/origins.yaml"
+  cp "$ROOT/.claude/loa/reference/hooks-reference.md" "$T/hooks-reference.md"
+  A="$T/audit.jsonl"
+  row() {  # ts pattern cwd command [extra-json]
+    jq -cn --arg ts "$1" --arg p "$2" --arg cwd "$3" --arg c "$4" --argjson x "${5:-{\}}" \
+      '{ts: $ts, tool: "Bash", command: $c, exit_code: 2, cwd: $cwd, model: "claude-test-model", hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: $p, matched: "m"} + $x'
+  }
+  {
+    # live, inside the repo
+    row "2026-10-12T08:00:00Z" "FR-SZ2-REDIR" "$ROOT" "cat > .claude/x.md <<'EOF'"            # heredoc → likely FP
+    row "2026-10-12T09:00:00Z" "P2" "/srv/elsewhere/scratch" "git push --force origin topic"    # outside repo → likely FP
+    row "2026-10-12T10:00:00Z" "SP-1" "$ROOT" "br comments add bd-1 'note about spike/x merge'" # prose class, no verb → likely FP
+    row "2026-10-13T23:59:00Z" "FR-2-AMBIGUOUS" "$ROOT" "cd sub && rm -rf ./.cache"             # prose class WITH verb → real
+    # replays
+    row "2026-10-11T08:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~1" '{"replay": true}'        # flag
+    row "2026-10-11T09:00:00Z" "P3" "$T/scratch" "git reset --hard HEAD~2"                       # cwd under TMPDIR
+    row "2026-10-11T10:00:00Z" "P3" "/home/u/bats-run-42/repo" "git reset --hard HEAD~3"        # cwd /bats-run-
+    for s in 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09; do                                                  # burst: 10 in one minute
+      row "2026-10-09T10:00:${s}Z" "P2" "$ROOT" "git push --force origin main"
+    done
+    # outside the window
+    row "2026-08-01T08:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~9"
+    # implement-gate telemetry and ask
+    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:00:00Z", hook: "implement-gate", action: "telemetry", cwd: "x"}'
+    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:05:00Z", hook: "implement-gate", action: "ask", cwd: "x"}'
+    # a non-block row and an unparseable line
+    jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-12T11:10:00Z", tool: "Bash", command: "ls", cwd: "x"}'
+    printf 'this is not json\n'
+  } > "$A"
+  # the rotated segment holds the one real P3 catch
+  row "2026-10-10T09:00:00Z" "P3" "$ROOT" "git reset --hard HEAD~3" > "$A.1"
+  ARGS=(--now "$NOW" --audit-log "$A" --origins "$T/origins.yaml" --out "$T/guards.md" --yield-dir "$T/run" --hooks-ref "$T/hooks-reference.md")
+}
+teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }
+
+g() { jq -c --arg id "$1" '.guards[] | select(.id == $id) | [.blocks_30d, .likely_fp_30d, .telemetry_30d, .last_real_catch]' "$T/run/guard-yield.json"; }
+
+@test "GY-1 replay rows are excluded by flag, cwd and burst and counted in the header; the window and bad rows are honoured" {
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output" >&2; false; }
+  J="$T/run/guard-yield.json"
+  [ "$(jq '.audit_segments' "$J")" = "2" ]
+  [ "$(jq '.audit_rows_considered' "$J")" = "20" ]
+  [ "$(jq '.replay_rows_excluded' "$J")" = "13" ]
+  [ "$(jq -c '.replay_rows_by_rule' "$J")" = '{"flag":1,"cwd":2,"burst":10}' ]
+  [ "$(jq '.audit_rows_unparseable' "$J")" = "1" ]
+  [ "$(jq -c '.totals | [.blocks_30d, .real_blocks_30d, .likely_fp_30d, .telemetry_30d]' "$J")" = '[5,2,3,2]' ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.scope' "$J")" = "host" ]
+  [ "$(jq -r '.window_days' "$J")" = "30" ]
+}
+
+@test "GY-2 the rotated segment is read: its real P3 catch is counted and is the guard's last_real_catch" {
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(g fence:P3)" = '[1,0,0,"2026-10-10"]' ]
+}
+
+@test "GY-3 heredoc, scratch-path and prose-class blocks classify as likely false positives; a prose class with a destructive verb is real" {
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ "$(g fence:FR-SZ2-REDIR)" = '[1,1,0,"none in window"]' ]
+  [ "$(g fence:P2)" = '[1,1,0,"none in window"]' ]
+  [ "$(g fence:SP-1)" = '[1,1,0,"none in window"]' ]
+  [ "$(g fence:FR-2-AMBIGUOUS)" = '[1,0,0,"2026-10-13"]' ]
+  [ "$(g hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh)" = '[5,3,0,"2026-10-13"]' ]
+}
+
+@test "GY-4 last_real_catch and generated_at are day-granular; telemetry counts implement-gate rows; non-writers show n/a" {
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  J="$T/run/guard-yield.json"
+  [ "$(jq -r '.generated_at' "$J")" = "2026-10-14" ]
+  [ -z "$(jq -r '.guards[].last_real_catch' "$J" | grep -vE '^([0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}|none in window|n/a)$' || true)" ]
+  [ "$(g gate:implement-gate)" = '[0,0,2,"none in window"]' ]
+  [ "$(g hook:compliance/implement-gate.sh)" = '[0,0,2,"none in window"]' ]
+  [ "$(g hook:safety/zone-write-guard.sh)" = '[null,null,null,"n/a"]' ]
+  grep -qE '^\| hook:safety/zone-write-guard.sh \|.*\| n/a \| n/a \| n/a \| n/a \|$' "$T/run/guard-yield.md"
+}
+
+@test "GY-5 no command text, cwd, hostname or model name reaches guards.md, the yield files or the hooks table" {
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --hooks-table
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  # the hooks reference documents fence commands in its own prose; only the generated block is checked
+  awk '/^<!-- guard-register:begin -->$/,/^<!-- guard-register:end -->$/' "$T/hooks-reference.md" > "$T/hooks-block.md"
+  [ -s "$T/hooks-block.md" ]
+  for f in "$T/guards.md" "$T/run/guard-yield.md" "$T/run/guard-yield.json" "$T/hooks-block.md"; do
+    for needle in "reset --hard" "push --force" "rm -rf" "spike/x merge" "<<'EOF'" "/srv/elsewhere" "bats-run-42" "$T" "claude-test-model" "$(hostname)"; do
+      if grep -qF -- "$needle" "$f"; then echo "$f leaks '$needle'" >&2; false; fi
+    done
+  done
+}
+
+@test "GY-6 guards.md is structural: header counts, one table per kind, no timestamp, and identical whatever the audit log holds" {
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  n="$(yq '.guards | length' "$T/origins.yaml")"
+  grep -qx -- "- guards: $n" "$T/guards.md"
+  grep -qx -- "- guards_without_origin: 0" "$T/guards.md"
+  grep -qx -- "- dormant: 3" "$T/guards.md"
+  for k in hook fence validator gate policy; do grep -qE "^## $k \([0-9]+\)$" "$T/guards.md"; done
+  [ "$(grep -cE '^\| (hook|fence|validator|gate|policy):' "$T/guards.md")" -eq "$n" ]
+  ! grep -qE '20[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T|generated_at' "$T/guards.md"
+  cp "$T/guards.md" "$T/guards.first"
+  : > "$A"; rm -f "$A.1"
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  cmp "$T/guards.first" "$T/guards.md"
+}
+
+@test "GY-7 --check exits 0 after generation, 1 after an origin edit (with the regenerate hint), 0 after a yield-only change" {
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --hooks-table
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --check
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  # yield-only change: more audit rows, regenerate the yield; the structure is untouched
+  jq -cn '{ts: "2026-10-14T08:00:00Z", hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: "block", pattern_id: "P4", cwd: "/x", command: "git clean -fd"}' >> "$A"
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --check
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  # origin edit
+  yq -i '(.guards[] | select(.id == "fence:P3") | .origin.ref) = "cycle-011 edited"' "$T/origins.yaml"
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --check
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"drift"*"guards.md"* ]]
+  [[ "$output" == *"regenerate: .claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh --hooks-table"* ]]
+  # a purpose edit drifts the hooks table too
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
+  yq -i '(.guards[] | select(.id == "hook:safety/notes-size-guard.sh") | .note) = "edited purpose"' "$T/origins.yaml"
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --check
+  [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"guard-register table"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GY-8 --hooks-table writes one row per registration between the markers, including the six hooks the hand table omitted" {
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --hooks-table
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  block="$(awk '/^<!-- guard-register:begin -->$/,/^<!-- guard-register:end -->$/' "$T/hooks-reference.md")"
+  regs="$(jq '[.hooks | to_entries[] | .value[] | .hooks[]] | length' "$ROOT/.claude/settings.json")"
+  [ "$(grep -E '^\| [A-Za-z]+ \|' <<<"$block" | grep -cv '^| Event |')" -eq "$regs" ]
+  for s in safety/zone-write-guard.sh safety/spiral-dispatch-guard.sh safety/spiral-skill-sentinel.sh safety/adversarial-review-gate.sh quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh scripts/upgrade-health-check.sh scripts/permission-audit.sh; do
+    grep -qF "$s" <<<"$block" || { echo "hooks table misses $s" >&2; false; }
+  done
+  grep -qE '^\| PreToolUse \| Bash \| `hook-guard.sh safety/team-role-guard.sh` \| dormant \| LOA_TEAM_MEMBER \|' <<<"$block"
+  grep -qE '^\| PreToolUse \| Write\\\|Edit\\\|MultiEdit\\\|NotebookEdit \|' <<<"$block"
+}
+
+@test "GY-9 --json prints the yield object (header, totals and one row per guard)" {
+  run --separate-stderr bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}" --json
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  n="$(yq '.guards | length' "$T/origins.yaml")"
+  jq -e --argjson n "$n" '
+    (keys | contains(["schema_version","generated_at","window_days","scope","audit_segments","audit_rows_considered","replay_rows_excluded","replay_rows_by_rule","heuristic","totals","guards"]))
+    and (.guards | length) == $n
+    and all(.guards[]; has("id") and has("class") and has("status") and has("origin") and has("knob") and has("floor") and has("registrations") and has("blocks_30d") and has("likely_fp_30d") and has("telemetry_30d") and has("last_real_catch"))
+    and (.totals | has("real_blocks_30d") and has("likely_fp_30d"))' <<<"$output" >/dev/null
+}
+
+@test "GY-10 a missing audit log is a WARN and an empty yield (exit 0); a missing origin row is exit 5" {
+  run bash "$GY" --now "$NOW" --audit-log "$T/none.jsonl" --origins "$T/origins.yaml" --out "$T/guards.md" --yield-dir "$T/run"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"WARN: no audit log"* ]]
+  [ "$(jq '.audit_rows_considered + .totals.blocks_30d' "$T/run/guard-yield.json")" = "0" ]
+  yq -i 'del(.guards[] | select(.id == "hook:safety/notes-size-guard.sh"))' "$T/origins.yaml"
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
+  [ "$status" -eq 5 ]
+  [[ "$output" == *"guard hook:safety/notes-size-guard.sh has no origin row"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "GY-11 a 10,000-row audit log is joined in under 10 seconds" {
+  jq -cn --arg r "$ROOT" 'range(10000) | {ts: "2026-10-12T08:\(. % 60 | tostring | if length == 1 then "0" + . else . end):00Z", hook: "block-destructive-bash", action: (if . % 2 == 0 then "block" else "allow-marker" end), pattern_id: "P2", cwd: $r, command: "git push --force origin b\(.)"}' > "$A"
+  rm -f "$A.1"
+  start=$(date +%s)
+  run bash "$GY" "${ARGS[@]}"
+  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+  [ $(( $(date +%s) - start )) -lt 10 ]
+}
diff --git a/tests/unit/loa-status-guards.bats b/tests/unit/loa-status-guards.bats

+++ b/tests/unit/loa-status-guards.bats
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/loa-status-guards.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 1 (PRD AC-1.5, SDD D-1.5)
+# `/loa` prints one Guards line: register counts from grimoires/loa/guards.md and
+# the 30-day host yield from .run/guard-yield.json (never recomputed at status
+# time), or the regenerate hint when the yield file is missing. Fixture files via
+# the bats-gated LOA_STATUS_GUARDS_FILE / LOA_STATUS_GUARD_YIELD_FILE seams.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  umask 022
+  export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1
+  PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+  STATUS="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lsg.XXXXXX")"
+  mkdir -p "$T/run" "$T/env"
+  export LOA_STATUS_RUN_DIR="$T/run" LOA_STATUS_ENV_DIR="$T/env" LOA_STATUS_CONFIG_FILE="$T/no-loa-config.yaml"
+  printf '# Guard register\n\n- guards: 94\n- guards_without_origin: 0\n- dormant: 3\n- floor: 21\n' > "$T/guards.md"
+  jq -n '{schema_version: 1, generated_at: "2026-10-14", window_days: 30, scope: "host",
+          totals: {guards: 94, real_blocks_30d: 87, likely_fp_30d: 72}}' > "$T/guard-yield.json"

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# Path-scoped rule files (grimoires/loa/sdd.md D-3.1, DEC-0129): stash-safety.md and
+# skill-invariants.md carry `paths:` frontmatter, the frontmatter parses, and every glob
+# matches at least one tracked file of the kind the rule is about (git pathspec glob
+# semantics: `**` spans directories, `*` stays inside one).
+
+setup() {
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "${BATS_TEST_DIRNAME}/../.." && pwd)"
+    RULES="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/rules"
+    command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"
+}
+
+# The YAML between the first two '---' lines (empty when the file has none).
+frontmatter() { awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" { exit } /^---$/ { if (n++) exit; next } n' "$1"; }
+globs() { frontmatter "$1" | yq eval '.paths[]' -; }
+tracked() { git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" ls-files -- ":(glob)$1"; }
+
+@test "RP-1 both rule files open with frontmatter that parses and lists string globs under paths:" {
+    local f n
+    for f in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
+        [ "$(head -1 "$RULES/$f")" = "---" ] || { echo "$f has no frontmatter"; return 1; }
+        frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.' - >/dev/null || { echo "$f frontmatter does not parse"; return 1; }
+        [ "$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.paths | type' -)" = "!!seq" ]
+        n="$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '.paths | length' -)"
+        [ "$n" -ge 1 ]
+        [ "$(frontmatter "$RULES/$f" | yq eval '[.paths[] | select(type != "!!str")] | length' -)" -eq 0 ]
+    done
+}
+
+@test "RP-2 the globs are the ones the SDD names" {
+    [ "$(globs "$RULES/stash-safety.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = '**/*.sh **/*.bats .claude/scripts/** .claude/hooks/** ' ]
+    [ "$(globs "$RULES/skill-invariants.md" | tr '\n' ' ')" = '.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md .claude/agents/** .claude/data/agent-types.yaml .claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities.sh ' ]
+}
+
+@test "RP-3 every stash-safety glob matches a tracked shell source" {
+    local g hits
+    while IFS= read -r g; do
+        hits="$(tracked "$g" | grep -E '\.(sh|bats)$' | head -1)"
+        [ -n "$hits" ] || { echo "glob '$g' matches no tracked .sh/.bats file"; return 1; }
+    done < <(globs "$RULES/stash-safety.md")
+}
+
+@test "RP-4 every skill-invariants glob matches a tracked skill, agent definition or capability file" {
+    local g hits
+    while IFS= read -r g; do
+        hits="$(tracked "$g" | grep -E '(^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$|^\.claude/agents/[^/]+\.md$|^\.claude/data/agent-types\.yaml$|^\.claude/scripts/validate-skill-capabilities\.sh$)' | head -1)"
+        [ -n "$hits" ] || { echo "glob '$g' matches no tracked file of the intended kind"; return 1; }
+    done < <(globs "$RULES/skill-invariants.md")
+}
+
+@test "RP-5 path-scoping removed no rule text: the body after the frontmatter keeps its heading and sections" {
+    local body
+    body="$(awk '/^---$/ && c < 2 { c++; next } c >= 2' "$RULES/stash-safety.md")"
+    [[ "$body" == *"# Git Stash Safety"* && "$body" == *"## Judgment rules the fence cannot express"* ]]
+    body="$(awk '/^---$/ && c < 2 { c++; next } c >= 2' "$RULES/skill-invariants.md")"
+    [[ "$body" == *"# Skill Frontmatter Invariants"* && "$body" == *"## The invariant"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "RP-6 the rule-lifecycle validator accepts both files (origin, version, enacted_by)" {
+    run "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/validate-rule-lifecycle.sh" --json
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$output"; return 1; }
+}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# heredoc-classifier.sh — library entry points for the FR-6 heredoc consumer
# classifier (cycle-129 D-6.1). The single implementation lives in the fence,
# .claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh; this file sources it in
# library mode (BDB_LIB_ONLY=1, which the fence honours only when sourced) so
# other scripts — guard-yield.sh's likely-false-positive heuristic — can call:
#
#   heredoc_consumer_class <command text>   prints interpreter|nonexec|none
#   heredoc_nonexec <command text>          exit 0 iff the command's heredocs
#                                           all have non-executing consumers
#
# Source only; never execute. Bash 3.2 compatible. When the fence cannot be
# read the functions report "none" / exit 1, which callers treat as "no
# classifier" (guard-yield.sh falls back to `<<` presence).
_hc_lib_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_hc_fence="${_hc_lib_dir}/../../hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh"
if [[ -r "$_hc_fence" ]]; then
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  BDB_LIB_ONLY=1 source "$_hc_fence"
fi
unset _hc_lib_dir _hc_fence

heredoc_consumer_class() {
  if declare -F _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _bdb_heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}"
  else
    printf 'none\n'
  fi
}

heredoc_nonexec() {
  [[ "$(heredoc_consumer_class "${1:-}")" == nonexec ]]
}

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (the PR description, `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is sprint-255: the guard register (`guard-yield.sh`, `guard-origins.yaml`, `floor.yaml`, the generated hooks table), the task-kind rule in `validate-artifact.sh` plus `tools/cycle-ratio.sh`, pre-registered control arms for the eval harness (`execute-agent.sh`, `run-arms.sh`, `arms-report.py`, `seed-corpus-from-record.sh`, `compare-ab.py`) and path-scoped rule files. 81 files, about 8,000 diff lines.

What was verified, not just read: I composed the head files over a framework checkout and executed the new code. `guard-yield.sh --hooks-table` regenerates the committed `hooks-reference.md` block byte for byte; `guard-yield.bats` passes 11/11, `guard-origins.bats` 14/15 (GO-9 fails only because `grimoires/loa/guards.md` is outside this fixture's scope), `validate-artifact-sprint-kinds.bats` 11/11, `rule-paths.bats` 6/6, `cycle-ratio.bats` 6/6, `loa-status-guards.bats` 3/3, `arms-report.bats` 7/7, `arm-toggles.bats` 11/11, `recall-baseline-freshness.bats` BF-10..13 4/4, `eval-recall-grader.bats` RG-28 passes (RG-17 needs the corpus directory, absent here). `sprint-seams.bats` SEAMS-9 and `seed-corpus.bats` need fixtures or graders that are not in this change set and could not be run.

The code is careful and well tested. One defect blocks: the `rule_files` control-arm toggle does not honour the harness's own invariant that an arm never silently runs as its baseline (Changes Required §1). The remaining findings are non-blocking observations, including a reproduced silent exit in `guard-yield.sh` when its optional heredoc library is present, and three functions over the complexity thresholds.

Process note: the implementation report (`pr/PR.md`) carries no `## AC Verification` walkthrough; per the review instructions for this frozen PR that pre-flight is skipped and not counted here.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Control-arm contract: `rule_files` toggle can run an arm as its baseline

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:266` — when neither `stash-safety.md` nor `skill-invariants.md` exists in the sandbox, the `rule_files` toggle records `removed: none present` and continues; the `no_rule_files` arm then runs identically to `baseline`, which the header at `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:65` says is exit 2 ("a toggle that cannot take effect is exit 2 (an arm never silently runs as its baseline)").
**File:** `head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:260-267`
**Issue:** Rules are materialised only when the prompt tree has them (`head/evals/harness/execute-agent.sh:146`, `if [[ -d "$PROMPT_TREE/.claude/rules" ]]`). A `--source-commit` that predates the two rule files, or any tree without `.claude/rules/`, makes the toggle a no-op. The post-check at line 264 only asserts absence, which is trivially true. The other three toggles (`companion_voice`, `karpathy_block`, `audit_delta_instruction`) fail closed when they find nothing to remove; this one does not. `arm-toggles.bats` AT-9 covers the fail-closed path for the other toggles but not this one.
**Why This Matters:** The pre-registered verdict in `arms-report.py` reads `no recall loss` for an arm whose only difference from baseline is the evidence string, and `arm_evidence` never reaches the report. SDD D-2.1 and `evals/README.md` say an arm verdict may license removing a control; a null experiment on the rule files would license deleting them. This is exactly the failure the "never silently runs as its baseline" invariant exists to prevent.
**Required Fix:** Fail the trial when nothing was removed, matching the other toggles, and add the AT-9-style case for it:
```bash
# Current (problematic)
_evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"

# Should be
[[ -n "$gone" ]] || { echo "ERROR: rule_files toggle: no rule file present in the sandbox .claude/rules/" >&2; return 2; }
_evidence rule_files "removed:$gone"
```
**Reference:** SDD D-2.1 (toggle contract); `evals/README.md` "Control arms and the record corpus" ("fails the trial (exit 2) when a toggle cannot take effect").

---

## Observations

Non-blocking. Medium and low findings, each with a concrete scenario.

### 1. Robustness of the guard register generator

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:470` — `source "$HEREDOC_LIB"` runs the library in the generator's own process; a library whose top level exits (or sources something that does) ends `guard-yield.sh` with exit 0, no output and nothing written. Reproduced: with the later-cycle `heredoc-classifier.sh` (which sources the fence) beside this PR's fence, every write-mode run and 7 of 11 `guard-yield.bats` cases silently produced no `guards.md` or yield file while reporting success. The script names a file it does not own as its optional dependency; evaluate the classifier in a subshell (or a `bash -c` helper that prints the indices) so a side effect in the library cannot terminate the generator, and treat "no files written" as a failure.
**Suggestion:** Run the `heredoc_nonexec` loop inside `( source "$HEREDOC_LIB"; ... )` and check `[[ -f "$YIELD_DIR/guard-yield.json" ]]` before the success line.
**Benefit:** An operator regenerating the register cannot be told "wrote" when nothing was written.

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:523` — `"fence:" + .pattern_id` adds a string to the raw field; a row whose `pattern_id` is a JSON number (`5` passes the `tostring | test(...)` guard) makes jq abort the whole join and the script exits 3 for one odd row. Use `("fence:" + (.pattern_id | tostring))`.

- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:443` — `"$AUDIT_LOG".*` also matches `audit.jsonl.lock`, `audit.jsonl.tmp` or editor leftovers beside the log; their contents are read as rows and inflate `audit_rows_unparseable`. Restrict to rotated segments (for example `"$AUDIT_LOG".[0-9]*`).

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:8` — the header says "one row per unique script" for hooks, but `render_hooks_block` emits one row per registration (`write-mutation-logger.sh` appears twice in the generated table, as GY-8 asserts). Fix the comment.

### 2. Floor design gap (cross-model DISS-C-001, confirmed)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/data/guard-origins.yaml:163` — the fence hook row `hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh` is `floor: false` while its sixteen `fence:FR-SZ*`/`FR-1.2b` rows are `floor: true` (`head/.claude/data/floor.yaml:14-41`). A change that drops the fence's `PreToolUse:Bash` registration from `settings.json` and its hook row from the map together passes `guard-yield.sh --check` (no dangling row), `guard-origins.bats` (floor rows unchanged; the markers still resolve in the script) and the corpus replay (which executes the script directly). `floor-snapshot.bats` FS-3 catches it only when `origin/main` is reachable, and it skips otherwise. Add `hook:safety/block-destructive-bash.sh` (and its registration) to `floor_guards`, or make `guard-yield.sh` refuse when a floor fence has no registered hook.

### 3. Path-scoped rule semantics (cross-model DISS-C-004, confirmed)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/rules/stash-safety.md:2-6` — the `paths:` globs scope the rule to sessions that touch `*.sh`, `*.bats`, `.claude/scripts/**` or `.claude/hooks/**`. The rule governs `git stash` commands the model issues through Bash, which happen in sessions editing only Markdown or YAML too; in those sessions the rule is no longer in context and only the FR-1.2b fence (swallowed-output shapes) remains. If the scoping is deliberate (DEC-0129), record that the unswallowed stash-wrap guidance is now fence-only and cover it with the `no_rule_files` arm result before relying on it.

### 4. Complexity (skill thresholds)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/arms-report.py:176-343` — `suite_report` is 168 lines with nesting over three deep (`for a in order` → `else` → `if reasons … else` → `if not violated … elif`) and no early returns. Split the per-arm verdict (lines 247-305) into a function returning `(verdict, reasons)` and the table/missed-labels rendering into another.
- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:976-1064` — `validate_sprint_kinds` is 89 lines; the embedded awk parser (lines 1004-1042) duplicates the task-line scanner in `head/tools/cycle-ratio.sh:46-66` (same section-state machine and token regex). Factor the scanner into `lib/` (as `md-fence.awk` already is) so the validator and the release-notes tool cannot drift.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:319-384` — `run_trial` is 66 lines with a retry loop four levels deep; extract the attempt body.

`SIMPLICITY`: no over-engineering beyond the above. net: -60 lines possible (shared scanner, split report).

### 5. Smaller defects

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/loa-status.sh:956` — every `jq -er` failure, including a present-but-malformed `guard-yield.json` or a schema drift between writer and reader, prints `no yield file (.run/guard-yield.json)`. LSG-3 pins this. Say "unreadable yield file" when the file exists so an operator does not regenerate in vain and a schema mismatch is visible.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/evals/harness/run-arms.sh:314` — `is_transport_failure` greps agent stderr and output for `network` and `5[0-9][0-9] ` anywhere; a review that mentions "network" or a line number like "line 503 " in the model's own output classifies a genuine agent failure as transport and costs a `--retry-wait` (default 300 s) retry. Anchor the patterns to the CLI's error lines.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/skills/implementing-tasks/SKILL.md:28` — the app zone flips from `read` to `read-write` with no mention in the PR description or title (SURGICAL). The change is probably right for `/implement`, but it changes what `validate-skill-capabilities.sh` and the zone reviewers see; state it, or move it to its own change.
- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/.github/workflows/check-prompt-budget.yml:5` — the header comment now states 160,000 B / 114,688 B while `tools/check-prompt-budget.sh` is not in this change set; PB-10 (`head/tests/unit/prompt-budget.bats:116-128`) pins the comment to the tool's constants, so this is only a defect if the tool still says 200,000 / 143,360. Could not verify here.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:528` — replay tagging reads the ambient `LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY`; a shell profile or a parent process that exports it marks every live block `replay: true` and the yield under-reports real catches (DISS-C-005). Consider requiring a second marker the harness alone sets (for example the sandbox cwd rule already in `guard-yield.sh`).

### 6. Change-set completeness (cannot verify from the fixture)

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: low) `head/.github/workflows/bats-tests.yml:159` — the new CI gate runs `guard-yield.sh --check`, which exits 1 when `grimoires/loa/guards.md` is absent (`head/.claude/scripts/guard-yield.sh:422`), and that tracked register is not in this change set. `seed-corpus-from-record.sh` excludes `grimoires/` from fixtures (`head/evals/harness/seed-corpus-from-record.sh:307`), so the real PR very likely carries it; confirm the register is committed and in sync, or the first CI run after merge is red.
- **LOW** (confidence: low) `head/evals/tasks/review-recall/review-pr-11.yaml:5` — the sixteen new tasks reference fixtures `review-prs/pr-11` … `pr-18`, hidden manifests and labels that are not in this change set; `run-arms.sh` refuses a missing fixture or manifest (exit 2). Same caveat about fixture scope.

Review complete. The feedback file is written and its trailer self-checks as consistent.

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** for the sprint-255 PR, on one high finding.

**The blocking defect** is in the control-arm harness. The `rule_files` toggle in `evals/harness/execute-agent.sh` records "removed: none present" and keeps going when neither rule file exists in the sandbox. Rules are only materialised when the prompt tree has a rules directory, so on an older source commit the `no_rule_files` arm runs identically to baseline. The script's own header promises exit 2 for exactly that case, and the arms report would then print "no recall loss" for a null experiment. The fix is a two-line fail-closed check plus a test case.

**What I verified by running code**, not just reading it. I composed the head files over the framework checkout and executed the new suites. The generated hooks table matches the committed one byte for byte. Results:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| guard-yield, kinds, rule-paths, cycle-ratio, loa-status-guards | all pass |
| arms-report, arm-toggles, compare BF-10..13, grader RG-28 | all pass |
| guard-origins | 14/15, the miss needs `grimoires/loa/guards.md`, which is outside the fixture's scope |

**Non-blocking observations** (6 medium, 10 low) include a reproduced silent exit in the register generator when its optional heredoc library is present, a floor-design gap where the fence hook row is not itself floor, the stash-safety rule now scoped to shell-file sessions although it governs Bash `git stash` usage, and three functions over the complexity thresholds. Two items are flagged low-confidence because the fixture excludes `grimoires/` and the record corpus, so I could not confirm the CI gate's register or the pr-11 to pr-18 fixtures are in the real change set.

**Cross-model dissent** ran clean with two independent voices and five advisory findings. Four were confirmed and folded into the observations. One, about a dependency-marker parser, was checked and found not to be a defect.

Outputs: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md` with the LOA-VERDICT trailer, plus `review.md` at the repo root in the brief's one-finding-per-line shape. Next step is the engineer's fix and a re-review.
